bottom_line: In patients with acute coronary syndromes without ST-segment elevation, clopidogrel plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin reduced the first primary outcome (relative risk, 0.80; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90).
implications: Based on the reported event rates (9.3% vs 11.4%) and relative risk (0.80; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.72 to 0.90; P<0.001), the document supports that adding clopidogrel to aspirin reduced the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or stroke in this trial population, while major bleeding was increased (3.7% vs 2.7%; relative risk, 1.38; P=0.001); the document also reports no significant excess in life-threatening bleeding (2.2% vs 1.8%; P=0.13).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing clopidogrel with placebo in ACS without ST-segment elevation.
major_points.quote: We undertook a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing clopidogrel with placebo in patients who presented with acute coronary syndromes without ST-segment elevation.

major_points.text: 12,562 patients were randomized within 24 hours after symptom onset to clopidogrel (loading then daily) or placebo, in addition to aspirin, for 3 to 12 months.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 12,562 patients who had presented within 24 hours after the onset of symptoms to receive clopidogrel (300 mg immediately, followed by 75 mg once daily) (6259 patients) or placebo (6303 patients) in addition to aspirin for 3 to 12 months.

major_points.text: The first primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The first primary outcome was the composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or stroke

major_points.text: Major bleeding was more common with clopidogrel than placebo (3.7% vs 2.7%; relative risk 1.38; P=0.001).
major_points.quote: There were significantly more patients with major bleeding in the clopidogrel group than in the placebo group (3.7 percent vs. 2.7 percent; relative risk, 1.38; P=0.001)

absolute_effects.text: Second primary outcome: 1035 (16.5) vs 1187 (18.8) (clopidogrel vs placebo).
Total with bleeding complications: 533 (8.5) vs 317 (5.0) (clopidogrel vs placebo).

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses were conducted with tests for interactions in the Cox regression model.
subgroups.quote: Subgroup analyses were conducted with the use of tests for interactions in the Cox regression model.

subgroups.text: Greater benefit tendency among patients with previous revascularization (RR 0.56) than those who had not (RR 0.88); P for interaction=0.002.
subgroups.quote: There was a tendency to- ward a greater benefit among patients who had pre- viously undergone revascularization (relative risk of the first primary outcome, 0.56; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.43 to 0.72) than among those who had not (relative risk, 0.88; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.78 to 0.99; P for interaction=0.002).

harms.text: Major bleeding occurred in 3.7% vs 2.7% (clopidogrel vs placebo), RR 1.38 (95% CI 1.13–1.67).
Life-threatening bleeding: 2.2% vs 1.8% (clopidogrel vs placebo), RR 1.21 (95% CI 0.95–1.56).
Minor bleeding: 5.1% vs 2.4% (clopidogrel vs placebo), RR 2.12 (1.75–2.56).
Permanent discontinuation of study medication: 21.1% vs 18.8% (clopidogrel vs placebo).
harms.quote: A total of 21.1 percent of the patients in the clopidogrel group discontinued the study med- ication permanently, as compared with 18.8 percent in the placebo group.

inclusion_criteria.text: Hospitalized within 24 hours after the onset of symptoms and did not have ST-segment elevation.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible for the study if they had been hospital- ized within 24 hours after the onset of symptoms and did not have ST-segment elevation.

inclusion_criteria.text: After a review, enrollment was limited to patients with either electrocardiographic changes or an elevation in serum cardiac enzymes or markers at entry.
inclusion_criteria.quote: the steering committee recommended that we enroll only patients who had ei- ther electrocardiographic changes or an elevation in the serum level of cardiac enzymes or markers at entry.

exclusion_criteria.quote: We excluded patients with contraindications to antithrombotic or antiplatelet therapy

analysis_methods.text: For first primary outcome: assuming 10% placebo rate and two-sided alpha 0.045, 12,500 patients would have 90% power to detect 16.9% risk reduction.
analysis_methods.quote: Assuming a rate of 10 percent in the placebo group for the first pri- mary outcome and a two-sided alpha level of 0.045, a study with 12,500 patients would have 90 percent power to detect a 16.9 per- cent reduction in risk.

analysis_methods.text: Alpha partitioning maintained overall level 0.05 after adjustment for overlap between outcome sets.
analysis_methods.quote: Partitioning the alpha maintains an overall level of 0.05, after adjustment for the overlap between the two sets of outcomes.

analysis_methods.text: All analyses were based on the intention-to-treat principle.
analysis_methods.quote: All analyses were based on the inten- tion-to-treat principle

analysis_methods.text: Analyses used either the log-rank statistic or the chi-square test.
analysis_methods.quote: used either the log-rank statistic or the chi-square test.

analysis_methods.text: Two formal interim assessments were performed at approximately one third and two thirds of expected events.
analysis_methods.quote: There were two formal interim assess- ments performed at the times when approximately one third and two thirds of the expected events had occurred.

trial_conduct.quote: The ethics review board at each institution approved the study.

trial_conduct.text: Independent data and safety monitoring board periodically reviewed the data.
trial_conduct.quote: The data were periodically reviewed by an independent data and safety monitoring board.

trial_conduct.text: Primary outcomes and life-threatening and major bleeding were adjudicated by persons unaware of treatment assignments.
trial_conduct.quote: All primary outcomes and life-threatening and major bleeding complications were adjudicated by persons who were unaware of the patients’ treatment-group assignments.

trial_conduct.text: Data and safety monitoring board monitored primary outcome for benefit using a modified Haybittle–Peto boundary.
trial_conduct.quote: The data and safety monitoring board monitored the incidence of the primary outcome to determine the benefit of clopidogrel, using a modified Haybittle–Peto boundary

trial_conduct.text: Despite crossing the preset efficacy boundary by the second interim analysis, the board recommended the trial continue to planned end.
trial_conduct.quote: Despite the fact that the preset boundary indicating efficacy had been crossed by the time of the second interim analysis, the board recommended that the trial continue until its planned end
